Subject: Hosted API: post-demo cost walkthrough & next steps

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciated the thoughtful questions. Quick recap and the items we discussed for pricing qualification so your procurement and engineering teams can evaluate cost: 

Summary of what we saw:
- Hosted API (low lift) with streaming response option and token-level billing.
- Example integration pattern: client-side prompt -> Redwood hosted endpoint -> structured JSON output.

We agreed to confirm the following to finalize a hosted pricing estimate:
1) Expected average monthly token volume (input + output) — a range is fine (low/typical/high).
2) Peak TPS (tokens/sec) target during daily peaks and any burst windows.
3) Target budget band (monthly) or target $/1M tokens to guide discounting.
4) Latency SLOs (p95) for the most critical endpoints (if <300ms we should know).
5) Any compliance items: regions, data residency.

What I captured on the call (please correct):
- Use case: in-app clinical triage and note summarization (mix of short prompts and longer outputs, average response ~800 tokens).
- Primary integration: hosted API, start with Redwood-managed models; may evaluate Dedicated later if volumes grow.

Attached: rough hosted pricing estimate spreadsheet (left column is baseline list price; right column shows example cost at a few volume bands). Also included a short MAP-terms draft to speed procurement review.

Next steps / asks: 
- Maria/Evan: please reply with the ranges for items 1–3 above by EOD tomorrow so we can lock an initial quote.
- Ben: I’m cc’ing you to help with unit-econ questions and to translate to a 90-day forecast for the finance team.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short follow-up if that’s easier.

Best,

Thanks Hannah — great session. A few clarifications and our initial numbers below. Evan and I pulled these from our telemetry and product roadmap: 

1) Monthly token volume (input+output):
- Low: ~120M tokens/month (pilot, limited region)
- Typical: ~650M tokens/month (expected after Q1 ramp)
- High: ~1.2B tokens/month (full rollout across two regions)

2) Peak TPS (tokens/sec) during busy windows:
- Baseline peak: 45 TPS (sustained for ~10 minutes during daily peak)
- Burst: up to 220 TPS for short, 30–60s bursts tied to health check-ins and push notifications

3) Budget band / target unit price:
- Procurement is aiming for $600–$1,200 per 1M tokens depending on SLA/package. Internal target is closer to $800/1M but there is some flexibility if latency and availability align.

Latency: p95 target for triage endpoint is <= 600ms; non-blocking background tasks can be higher.

Compliance: data must remain in us-west and us-east regions; SOC2 + HIPAA controls required (we’ll send the questionnaire next).

Next steps from our side: Evan will pull a 90-day usage forecast that shows ramp by customer cohort. We expect to share that by EOD Friday (2026-09-18).

Happy to review your attached estimate after Ben tees up the unit-econ view.

—Maria

Subject: Internal: quick unit-econ sketch for ClearSky (do not forward)

Hannah — quick note following Maria’s numbers. I sketched a few price points in the attached worksheet and a short sensitivity table. Key assumptions below: 

Assumptions
- Average tokens per request: 850 (Maria said ~800 average response + prompt).
- Effective happy-path loss (KV cache / system-level dedupe) gives ~15% fewer billable tokens in practice for triage flows.
- Baseline list price (no discount): $1,500 / 1M tokens.

Sensitivity highlights
- If ClearSky targets $800 / 1M, margin to Redwood (considering infra + infra amort) is narrow for hosted; recommend offering a 6–9 month ramp plan with minimum monthly commit to protect unit economics.
- For volumes >= 1B tokens/mo, propose a Dedicated evaluation (or large hosted commit) — gives us room to hit $400–700 / 1M net.

Suggested next step
- Propose we share a 3-tier hosted quote (pilot / ramp / committed) with clear versioning and a canary fallback to a lower-cost model if latency SLOs aren’t met. I’ll draft the numbers and have a clean Q sheet by EOD.

LMK if you want me to join the call with procurement tomorrow.

—Ben
